question:
I have this override of the ref macro in a file in the macros/ folder of my dbt project.

{%- macro ref(table_name) -%}

    {% set relation = builtins.ref(table_name) %}
    {% do return(relation) %}

{%- endmacro -%}

When I try to run any model using dbt run --models xxx this results in the error below:

Encountered an error:
keyword argument repeated: tags (<template>, line 12)

If I delete the file then dbt models run as expected.

I expect this macro to return the dbt Relation object just like the original dbt source function.

Have also tried overriding the source macro with the same result:

{%- macro source(source_name, table_name) -%}

    {% set rel = builtins.source(source_name, table_name) %}
    {{ rel }}

{%- endmacro -%}

and

{%- macro source(source_name, table_name) -%}

    {% set rel = builtins.source(source_name, table_name) %}
    {% do return(rel) %}

{%- endmacro -%}

I have seen similar usage here - overriding the source function - that's exactly what I'm trying to do: https://medium.com/checkout-com-techblog/dbt-modeling-at-scale-2614202bb5d0

Running with:

dbt-core==1.6.6
dbt-refshift==1.6.2
Python 3.9.13

I have checked similar questions but these do not answer my question above, for example: Overriding source macro in DBT to allow for dynamic sources for test runs

Thanks in advance for any leads/advice!
title: Overriding dbt source function with a basic passthrough macro fails
answer: Just in case someone gets a similar error, in the config of one of the dbt models the 'tags' parameter was defined twice, that caused the error.
